properties.text: bytes_to_bls_field MUST reject any input whose deserialized integer is >= BLS_MODULUS. Modular reduction (silent wrapping) is not acceptable; the function must raise an error/revert.

reachability.notes: Attacker submits blob with field elements >= BLS_MODULUS via type-3 transaction or provides crafted cells over P2P. If bytes_to_bls_field uses modular reduction instead of rejection, polynomial arithmetic produces incorrect but valid-looking results.

properties.severity_justification: Out-of-range field elements corrupt polynomial arithmetic, leading to invalid cells and proofs that may pass verification. Affects integrity of data availability guarantees.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that out-of-range field element input produces cells/proofs that pass verification but correspond to incorrect data.

properties.text: The Fiat-Shamir challenge in compute_verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_challenge MUST include ALL of: RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL, len(commitments), len(cell_indices), all commitment bytes, all commitment_indices, all cell_indices, all coset evaluations (serialized via bls_field_to_bytes), and all proof bytes, in deterministic canonical order.

reachability.notes: If any verifier-relevant data is omitted from the Fiat-Shamir hash, an attacker can manipulate the omitted field while keeping the challenge unchanged, breaking batch verification soundness.

properties.severity_justification: Breaking Fiat-Shamir soundness allows forging batch proofs, enabling invalid data to pass verification. This is a consensus-level failure affecting all nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that omitting or reordering hash input allows construction of a batch proof that passes verification for invalid data.

properties.text: The RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN separator MUST be unique across all Ethereum protocol contexts. No other Fiat-Shamir construction in the protocol may use the same domain separator.

reachability.notes: Domain separator collision would enable cross-protocol attacks where a valid proof in one context is accepted in the KZG cell batch context.

properties.severity_justification: Cross-protocol domain confusion could allow proof forgery across different verification contexts, undermining data availability guarantees.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate cross-protocol proof replay or domain collision with another Ethereum subsystem.

properties.text: The hash input order in compute_verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_challenge MUST be deterministic and canonical: domain separator, then FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL, len(commitments), len(cell_indices), then all commitments, then for each k: commitment_indices[k], cell_indices[k], all coset_evals elements, proofs[k].

reachability.notes: Non-deterministic ordering would allow different nodes to compute different challenges for the same inputs, enabling targeted proof forgery.

properties.severity_justification: Non-canonical ordering breaks Fiat-Shamir binding. Different challenge values for same logical inputs means verification is inconsistent across nodes, potentially causing consensus splits.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show that implementation uses non-canonical ordering and demonstrate divergent verification results.

properties.text: verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch MUST reject any cell_index >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB. The assertion must be enforced before accessing coset_for_cell or coset_shift_for_cell.

reachability.notes: Out-of-bounds cell_index causes array access beyond roots_brp bounds in coset_shift_for_cell (SG-016) and coset_for_cell (SG-017). Could crash the node or cause memory corruption in unsafe languages.

properties.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds access can crash the validator node (DoS) or in unsafe languages cause memory corruption. Attacker sends crafted data column sidecar via P2P with invalid cell_index.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate node crash or undefined behavior from out-of-bounds cell_index in a P2P message.

properties.text: All four input arrays to verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch (commitment_bytes, cell_indices, cells, proofs_bytes) MUST have equal length. The function MUST reject inputs where lengths differ.

reachability.notes: Mismatched array lengths could cause index-out-of-bounds during iteration over k in the batch verification loop.

properties.severity_justification: Mismatched lengths lead to out-of-bounds access during batch verification iteration, causing node crash.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show that a crafted P2P message with mismatched array lengths crashes the verifying node.

properties.text: Commitment deduplication in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch MUST use byte-exact comparison (not hash-based). Two commitment_bytes entries are duplicates if and only if they are byte-identical. The commitment_indices mapping must correctly map each original index to its position in the deduplicated list.

reachability.notes: Incorrect deduplication (hash collision or off-by-one in commitment_indices) causes weight aggregation errors in the random linear combination, potentially accepting invalid proofs.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect weight aggregation in the verification equation could allow invalid proofs to pass, breaking data availability verification for affected sidecars.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that deduplication error causes invalid proof acceptance via weight aggregation mismatch.

properties.text: The universal verification equation e(LL, LR) == e(RL, [1]) in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl MUST hold if and only if all individual cell proofs are valid. The equation MUST reject any batch containing at least one invalid cell proof with overwhelming probability (1 - 1/p where p is the BLS scalar field order).

reachability.notes: The random challenge r produced by hash_to_bls_field must have sufficient entropy. If the challenge has low entropy (weak hash, truncation), the probability of false acceptance increases.

properties.severity_justification: False acceptance of invalid proofs breaks data availability guarantees network-wide. Consensus failure: nodes disagree on validity of blocks.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that an invalid cell proof passes batch verification due to insufficient challenge entropy or equation aggregation error.

properties.text: bytes_to_kzg_commitment and bytes_to_kzg_proof MUST perform BLS12-381 G1 subgroup checks on deserialized points. Points not on the correct subgroup MUST be rejected before entering the pairing check.

reachability.notes: Without subgroup checks, an attacker can provide points on the wrong subgroup of BLS12-381. The pairing check would produce incorrect results, potentially accepting invalid proofs.

properties.severity_justification: Missing subgroup checks allow pairing-based proof forgery. This is a well-known attack vector in pairing-based cryptography that breaks all verification guarantees.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that a non-subgroup point causes the pairing check to accept an invalid proof.

properties.text: recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs MUST require at least CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2 cells (50% threshold) and at most CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells. Inputs with fewer cells MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: If the 50% threshold is not enforced, recovery with insufficient cells produces an incorrect polynomial. The Reed-Solomon rate-2 expansion requires at least half the cells.

properties.severity_justification: Recovery with insufficient cells produces incorrect polynomial, leading to invalid reconstructed cells and proofs that corrupt data availability.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that recovery with < 50% cells produces incorrect polynomial that generates invalid cells.

properties.text: recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs MUST require cell_indices to be unique and in ascending (sorted) order. Duplicate cell_indices MUST be rejected. Unsorted cell_indices MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: Duplicate cell_indices with conflicting cell data cause polynomial interpolation to produce incorrect results. An attacker providing duplicates with different cell content could trick recovery into producing a polynomial different from the original.

properties.severity_justification: Duplicate indices with conflicting data corrupt polynomial recovery, potentially causing the node to reconstruct and propagate invalid cells.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that duplicate cell_indices with conflicting data produce an incorrect recovered polynomial.

properties.text: The division by Z(x) in recover_polynomialcoeff MUST be performed on a coset shifted by PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY, not on the FFT domain. The vanishing polynomial Z(x) evaluates to zero on the FFT domain roots but MUST NOT evaluate to zero on any point of the coset.

reachability.notes: If the coset shift is incorrect (not PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY) or coincides with a root of Z(x), the element-wise division [a/b for a,b in zip(ez_over_coset, zp_over_coset)] will encounter division by zero, crashing the node.

properties.severity_justification: Division by zero crashes the validator node. An attacker who withholds specific columns can trigger recovery and the crash. Single-node DoS.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that specific withholding patterns combined with incorrect coset shift cause division by zero during recovery.

properties.text: The recovered polynomial from recover_polynomialcoeff MUST have degree strictly less than FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB. The truncation poly_coeff[:FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB] MUST discard only zero coefficients.

reachability.notes: If corrupted cells cause recovery to produce a polynomial with degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, the truncation silently discards non-zero high-degree coefficients, producing an incorrect polynomial.

properties.severity_justification: Silent truncation of non-zero coefficients produces incorrect polynomial, leading to invalid reconstructed cells that could propagate through the network.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that corrupted input cells cause high-degree coefficient truncation, producing incorrect reconstruction.

properties.text: After recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs produces reconstructed cells and proofs, the caller MUST verify the recovered polynomial against the original KZG commitment before accepting or propagating the results. The recovery function itself does NOT perform this verification.

reachability.notes: Corrupted cells produce incorrect polynomial. Without post-recovery commitment verification, the node becomes a vector for distributing invalid data. Other nodes trusting this node's reconstructed data would accept invalid cells.

properties.severity_justification: Node becomes an amplifier of invalid data if post-recovery verification is missing. Elevation of privilege: attacker uses honest node to distribute invalid sidecars.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that corrupted cells pass recovery and are propagated without commitment verification, causing other nodes to accept invalid data.

properties.text: The bit-reversal permutation in polynomial_eval_to_coeff, coset_for_cell, and coset_shift_for_cell MUST correctly implement the standard bit-reversal mapping: for an array of size N (power of 2), element at index i maps to index bit_reverse(i, log2(N)).

reachability.notes: Incorrect bit-reversal produces wrong polynomial coefficients from evaluations, causing all downstream cell computation and proof generation to be incorrect. Affects both blob processing and verification.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect bit-reversal corrupts all polynomial operations. While not directly attacker-triggered, the resulting invalid proofs would cause consensus divergence between correct and incorrect implementations.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that bit-reversal error produces cells/proofs inconsistent with the reference implementation.

properties.text: divide_polynomialcoeff MUST NOT accept a zero polynomial as divisor b. The leading coefficient b[bpos] MUST be nonzero. If b is the zero polynomial, the function MUST raise an error.

reachability.notes: Division by zero polynomial produces undefined results. In the recovery path (SG-023 -> SG-010), the vanishing polynomial is constructed from missing cell roots. If all cells are present (no missing), the vanishing polynomial should be handled as a special case.

properties.severity_justification: Division by zero polynomial causes crash or undefined behavior during polynomial recovery, resulting in validator node DoS.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that specific cell availability patterns lead to zero divisor polynomial and node crash.

properties.text: interpolate_polynomialcoeff MUST require all xs values to be distinct. If duplicate xs values are provided, the weight_adjustment computation (xs[i] - xs[j]).inverse() would attempt to invert zero. The function MUST detect and reject duplicate xs values.

reachability.notes: Duplicate coset points in interpolation arise from duplicate cell_indices (which should be caught by SG-024/INV-003). If the earlier check is bypassed, the inversion of zero crashes the node.

properties.severity_justification: Inversion of zero crashes the validator node. Defense-in-depth: even if SG-024 catches duplicates, the interpolation should also validate.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that duplicate xs values (from bypassed cell_index uniqueness check) cause crash in interpolation.

properties.text: multiply_polynomialcoeff MUST enforce that len(a) + len(b) <= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB before computing the product. If this assertion is violated, the product polynomial exceeds the extended evaluation domain.

reachability.notes: In the vanishing polynomial construction path (SG-022), iterative multiplication grows the polynomial. If too many missing cells are specified, the product could exceed bounds.

properties.severity_justification: Exceeding polynomial degree bounds corrupts subsequent FFT operations. Bounded by the maximum number of missing cells (CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2).
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that degree bound violation in multiply produces incorrect FFT results.

properties.text: The KZG trusted setup parameters KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL and KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL MUST be loaded from the canonical trusted setup and verified at node startup. The integrity of the SRS is the foundation of all KZG proof security.

reachability.notes: Trusted setup compromise is a protocol-level assumption, not an implementation bug. The ceremony's 1-of-N honesty assumption ensures the trapdoor is unknown.

properties.severity_justification: Compromised SRS allows forging all KZG proofs, completely breaking data availability. However, this is a protocol assumption, not an implementation issue.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Out of scope: trusted setup integrity is a protocol assumption, not an implementation vulnerability.

properties.text: compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs MUST reject any blob not exactly BYTES_PER_BLOB bytes in length. The assertion len(blob) == BYTES_PER_BLOB must be enforced before any polynomial conversion.

reachability.notes: Incorrectly sized blob causes incorrect slicing in cell_to_coset_evals, producing wrong field elements. Could also cause out-of-bounds reads.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect blob size primarily caught at transaction validation layer. If bypassed, causes incorrect polynomial conversion.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate blob size bypass leading to incorrect cell computation.

properties.text: cell_to_coset_evals MUST produce a CosetEvals with exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL elements, where each element is a valid BLS field element (< BLS_MODULUS). Each byte segment [i*BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT : (i+1)*BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT] must be exactly BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT bytes.

reachability.notes: Cells received over P2P are deserialized into coset evaluations. If cell byte length is not FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT, slicing produces incorrect field elements.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect deserialization produces wrong coset evaluations used in batch verification. Could cause false accept/reject of proofs.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show that malformed cell bytes produce incorrect coset evaluations affecting verification outcome.

properties.text: coset_evals_to_cell MUST produce a Cell of exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * BYTES_PER_FIELD_ELEMENT bytes, and MUST be the exact inverse of cell_to_coset_evals for valid field elements: cell_to_coset_evals(coset_evals_to_cell(evals)) == evals.

reachability.notes: Roundtrip invariant for cell serialization/deserialization. Violation would corrupt all cell handling but requires implementation bug, not external attack.

properties.severity_justification: Broken roundtrip corrupts all cell operations. However, this is a pure implementation correctness issue, not directly exploitable by external attacker.

properties.text: The FFT implementation (_fft_field) MUST require input length to be a power of 2 and MUST equal len(roots_of_unity). Recursive calls MUST halve the input size at each level.

reachability.notes: FFT input size is determined by protocol constants (FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB). Non-power-of-2 inputs would cause incorrect butterfly operations.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect FFT produces wrong polynomial coefficients/evaluations. Protocol constants should ensure power-of-2 sizes.

properties.text: When inv=True, fft_field MUST apply inverse FFT normalization factor 1/N (where N = len(vals)) and MUST reverse the roots_of_unity order (except first element). The normalization factor is computed as N^(-1) mod BLS_MODULUS.

reachability.notes: Missing normalization in inverse FFT produces coefficients scaled by N. This would corrupt all polynomial operations using inverse FFT.

properties.severity_justification: Missing inverse FFT normalization corrupts polynomial recovery and cell computation. All reconstructed data would be incorrect.

properties.text: coset_fft_field forward path MUST shift values by shift_factor (PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY) before FFT. Inverse path MUST FFT first then unshift by shift_factor.inverse(). The order of shift and FFT operations MUST NOT be reversed.

reachability.notes: Coset FFT is used in polynomial recovery (SG-023). Reversed order of shift/FFT produces incorrect coset evaluations, corrupting the division step.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect coset FFT operation order corrupts polynomial recovery. While implementation-level, it affects externally-triggered recovery path.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that incorrect coset FFT order produces wrong recovery results for valid cell inputs.

properties.text: polynomial_eval_to_coeff MUST correctly convert FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB evaluation-form values to coefficient-form. The input MUST have exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB evaluations. Bit-reversal permutation MUST be applied before inverse FFT.

reachability.notes: Blob data enters polynomial pipeline via this conversion. Incorrect conversion produces wrong polynomial coefficients, invalidating all cells and proofs.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong polynomial coefficients from conversion cause all downstream cell and proof computation to be incorrect.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that conversion error produces cells inconsistent with the reference specification.

properties.text: compute_kzg_proof_multi_impl MUST correctly compute the quotient polynomial Q(X) = (f(X) - I(X)) / Z(X) where Z vanishes on all evaluation points zs and I is the interpolation polynomial. The proof MUST be a commitment to Q(X) using KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL.

reachability.notes: KZG proof computation uses the quotient polynomial. Incorrect quotient produces invalid proofs that should be caught by verification but could cause consensus issues if the error is systematic.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect quotient polynomial produces invalid proofs. Systematic errors could cause all proofs from affected nodes to be invalid, leading to data availability failures.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that proof computation error produces proofs that fail batch verification.

properties.text: compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff MUST produce exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells and CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB proofs. Each proof MUST be valid for its corresponding cell evaluated on the cell's coset.

reachability.notes: If cell/proof count differs from CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB, downstream sidecar construction will produce incorrect sidecars with mismatched data.

properties.severity_justification: Wrong number of cells/proofs causes sidecar construction failures or mismatched data. Detected at sidecar verification by receiving nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate mismatch in cell/proof count causing sidecar construction or verification failure.

properties.text: The vanishing polynomial constructed by vanishing_polynomialcoeff MUST evaluate to 0 at every point in xs, MUST have degree exactly len(xs), and MUST be monic (leading coefficient is 1).

reachability.notes: Vanishing polynomial is constructed from missing cell roots during recovery. Incorrect vanishing polynomial corrupts the recovery division step.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect vanishing polynomial corrupts recovery but the final result should be caught by post-recovery commitment verification (PROP-0014).
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate vanishing polynomial incorrectness causing recovery failure.

properties.text: construct_vanishing_polynomial (SG-022) MUST require at least one cell to be present (not all cells can be missing). The coefficient spacing by FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL MUST correctly extend the short vanishing polynomial to the full domain.

reachability.notes: If all cells are missing, the vanishing polynomial equals the full domain polynomial, and recovery is impossible. The 50% threshold in SG-024 should prevent this.

properties.severity_justification: Edge case: if maximum missing cells boundary is reached, vanishing polynomial construction cost is maximized. Computational DoS bounded by 50% threshold.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate computational cost at boundary conditions of missing cell count.

properties.text: evaluate_polynomialcoeff MUST use Horner's method (or equivalent) to correctly compute sum(coeff[i] * z^i) for all i. The evaluation result MUST equal the mathematical definition of polynomial evaluation.

reachability.notes: Polynomial evaluation is used in KZG proof computation and cell computation. Incorrect evaluation produces wrong proofs and cells.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect polynomial evaluation corrupts all proof and cell computations. Fundamental correctness requirement.

properties.text: coset_shift_for_cell MUST return the correct coset generator h for the given cell_index, computed as roots_brp[FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL * cell_index] where roots_brp is the bit-reversal permutation of the roots of unity of order FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB.

reachability.notes: coset_shift_for_cell is used in batch verification (SG-015) to compute h_k.pow(n). Incorrect coset shift produces wrong verification equation terms.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect coset shift in verification equation corrupts the batch check. Could cause valid proofs to be rejected or invalid proofs to be accepted.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that coset shift error causes verification equation mismatch.

properties.text: coset_for_cell MUST return a Coset with exactly FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL elements. The coset elements MUST be the set {h, h*g, h*g^2, ...} where h = coset_shift_for_cell(cell_index) and g generates the subgroup of order FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL.

reachability.notes: Coset elements define the evaluation points for each cell. Incorrect coset elements produce cells that are inconsistent with the KZG commitment.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect coset definition makes cells inconsistent with commitments, but caught by verification.

properties.text: All commitment_indices in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl MUST reference valid entries in the deduplicated commitments list (commitment_indices[k] < len(commitments) for all k).

reachability.notes: If commitment_indices contain out-of-bounds values (due to deduplication bug), the weight accumulation weights[commitment_indices[k]] causes out-of-bounds access.

properties.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds commitment_indices cause crash or memory corruption during weight accumulation in batch verification.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that deduplication produces out-of-bounds commitment_indices causing crash.

properties.text: The deduplicated commitments list in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl MUST contain no duplicates. This is enforced by the deduplication step in SG-021.

reachability.notes: Duplicates in the commitments list passed to _impl would cause the g1_lincomb to produce incorrect RLC, breaking verification equation.

properties.severity_justification: Duplicates in the deduplicated list cause incorrect weight aggregation, potentially causing false acceptance of invalid proofs.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate duplicate commitments in _impl list causing verification equation to accept invalid proof.

properties.text: Each commitment_bytes entry in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch MUST be exactly BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT bytes. Each cell MUST be exactly BYTES_PER_CELL bytes. Each proof_bytes MUST be exactly BYTES_PER_PROOF bytes. Entries with incorrect lengths MUST be rejected.

reachability.notes: Incorrectly sized byte arrays cause deserialization errors or incorrect field element parsing. Must be caught before cryptographic operations.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect byte lengths cause deserialization errors that should be caught early. If not caught, could lead to incorrect cryptographic operations.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that incorrect byte lengths bypass validation and cause downstream errors.

properties.text: get_validators_custody_requirement MUST return a value in the range [VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT, NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS] inclusive. The clamping min(max(count, VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT), NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS) MUST be applied after the integer division.

reachability.notes: Custody requirement determines how many data column groups a validator must custody. Incorrect computation could cause validators to custody too few or too many groups.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect custody requirement weakens data availability sampling security guarantees. Validators custodying too few groups reduces the effective sampling rate.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Internal computation, not directly attacker-triggered via in-scope entry points.

properties.text: BALANCE_PER_ADDITIONAL_CUSTODY_GROUP MUST be a non-zero protocol constant. If it were zero, the integer division total_node_balance // BALANCE_PER_ADDITIONAL_CUSTODY_GROUP would cause a division-by-zero crash.

reachability.notes: Protocol constant validated at startup. Zero value would crash all validators during custody computation.

properties.severity_justification: Division by zero crashes all validators if constant is misconfigured. Protocol-level issue, not externally triggered.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Protocol constant misconfiguration, not externally exploitable.

properties.text: cells_and_kzg_proofs_construction (Validator SG-002) MUST require blobs_bundle.proofs to have length exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB * len(blobs_bundle.blobs). Proof slicing indices [start:end] where start = i * CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB and end = (i+1) * CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB MUST always be in bounds.

reachability.notes: Proofs from EL via Engine API. If proofs array is shorter than expected, slicing returns fewer proofs, causing mismatched cells and proofs in sidecars.

properties.severity_justification: Silent slicing of too-short proofs array produces sidecars with mismatched cells and proofs. Detected at verification by receiving nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires compromised EL (Engine API attacker_controlled: false). Conditional scope.

properties.text: get_data_column_sidecars MUST produce exactly NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS sidecars. Each sidecar MUST have sidecar.index == column_index matching its position. Each sidecar MUST contain one cell and one proof per blob.

reachability.notes: Incorrect number of sidecars or mismatched index values cause subnet routing errors and verification failures at receiving nodes.

properties.severity_justification: Mismatched sidecar.index causes sidecars to be published to wrong subnets or fail verification. Detected by receiving validators.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that index mismatch causes subnet routing error or verification failure.

properties.text: get_data_column_sidecars_from_column_sidecar MUST verify that len(cells_and_kzg_proofs) == len(sidecar.kzg_commitments) before delegating to get_data_column_sidecars. The signed_block_header, kzg_commitments, and kzg_commitments_inclusion_proof reused from the input sidecar MUST have been previously verified against the canonical chain.

reachability.notes: Attacker provides sidecar with forged signed_block_header and kzg_commitments. If not verified before reconstruction, the node produces and distributes sidecars linked to a non-existent or malicious block.

properties.severity_justification: Forged block header in reconstructed sidecars causes receiving nodes to accept data for non-existent blocks, corrupting data availability state.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate forged header propagation through sidecar reconstruction.

properties.text: Each data column sidecar MUST be published to exactly one subnet, deterministically computed from column_index via compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar. All NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS sidecars MUST be published before the proposer considers publishing complete.

reachability.notes: A malicious proposer can selectively withhold sidecars. The protocol relies on Reed-Solomon redundancy and data availability sampling to detect withholding. More than 50% withholding prevents recovery.

properties.severity_justification: Selective sidecar withholding prevents data availability verification. If > 50% withheld, recovery is impossible and the block should not be finalized.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that selective withholding of > 50% columns prevents recovery and finalization.

properties.text: Data column sidecars MUST be retained for at least MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS epochs. Sidecars MUST be served when requested during the retention period. Pruning MAY only occur after the retention period expires.

reachability.notes: Premature pruning prevents peers from obtaining sidecars for data availability sampling or cell recovery, potentially causing incorrect finality assessments.

properties.severity_justification: Premature pruning degrades data availability but is bounded by the retention period. Affects node's ability to serve DAS requests.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that premature pruning causes data availability sampling failure.

properties.text: Batch KZG verification via verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch MUST correctly detect spoofed data column sidecars with fabricated KZG commitments and cells from untrusted P2P peers. The pairing check e(LL, LR) == e(RL, [1]) MUST reject any sidecar where cells are inconsistent with the claimed commitments.

reachability.notes: Primary defense against spoofed sidecars. The verification equation must be sound: accept only if all individual cell proofs are valid.

properties.severity_justification: Failure to detect spoofed sidecars allows invalid data to be accepted as available, breaking consensus guarantees.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that a crafted spoofed sidecar passes batch verification.

properties.text: A malicious block proposer who modifies data column sidecars after valid computation (e.g., swapping cells between columns, providing mismatched column_index) MUST be detected by receiving validators via verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch and kzg_commitments_inclusion_proof verification against the block's Merkle root.

reachability.notes: Proposer-originated tampering requires receiving validators to independently verify each sidecar. The sidecar.index must match the expected column_index.

properties.severity_justification: Tampered sidecars from proposer could cause data corruption if verification is incomplete (e.g., skipping Merkle proof check).
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that tampered sidecar (swapped cells or mismatched index) passes incomplete verification.

properties.text: The E(x) * Z(x) identity in recover_polynomialcoeff MUST hold: the product of the extended evaluation polynomial and the vanishing polynomial on the FFT domain MUST equal the product of the original polynomial and the vanishing polynomial. This identity enables recovery without knowing the original polynomial directly.

reachability.notes: This algebraic identity is the mathematical foundation of the recovery algorithm. If the identity does not hold due to implementation error, recovery produces incorrect results.

properties.severity_justification: Violation of the algebraic identity means recovery always produces incorrect results, breaking data availability for all affected blobs.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that implementation does not correctly implement the E(x)*Z(x) = P(x)*Z(x) identity.

properties.text: The add_polynomialcoeff function MUST produce a result polynomial of degree max(deg(a), deg(b)). The shorter polynomial MUST be zero-padded for missing high-degree coefficients. No overflow beyond BLS_MODULUS may occur in coefficient addition.

reachability.notes: Polynomial addition is used extensively in recovery and proof computation. Incorrect addition corrupts all downstream operations.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect polynomial addition is a correctness issue affecting all polynomial operations. Not directly attacker-triggered.

properties.text: The computational complexity of compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs MUST be bounded. The reference specification uses O(n^2) complexity (SG-019/INV-003). Implementations SHOULD use FK20 algorithm for O(n log n) complexity. The protocol MUST limit the number of blobs per block to MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK to bound total computation.

reachability.notes: Attacker submits maximum number of blobs per block. O(n^2) implementations may experience significant delays during block processing. FK20 is preferred but not required.

properties.severity_justification: Computational DoS during block processing. Bounded by MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK but O(n^2) implementations are more vulnerable.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate measurable block processing delay from maximum blob throughput on O(n^2) implementation.

properties.text: Rate limiting MUST be applied to batch KZG verification of P2P-received data column sidecars. Cheap pre-checks (length validation, range checks on cell_indices) MUST be applied before expensive cryptographic operations (multi-scalar multiplication, interpolation, pairing check).

reachability.notes: Attacker sends large batches of invalid sidecars requiring full cryptographic verification before rejection. CPU exhaustion on verifying nodes.

properties.severity_justification: CPU exhaustion from processing many invalid sidecars. Mitigated by rate limiting and batch verification amortization.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate measurable CPU impact from crafted invalid sidecar batches that bypass cheap pre-checks.

properties.text: Timing side channels in KZG batch verification MUST NOT leak information about which commitments are cached, which cell_indices are locally available, or the structure of the verification batch. BLS field arithmetic and pairing computations MUST use constant-time implementations.

reachability.notes: Timing information could help an attacker target specific validators. Batch verification logic (weight accumulation, interpolation) may not be constant-time even if BLS operations are.

properties.severity_justification: Information disclosure via timing side channels. Useful for targeting but does not directly compromise consensus or data availability.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Conditional scope: requires further investigation of practical exploitability.

properties.text: Blob data encoded into Reed-Solomon cells is inherently public once included in a block. The data availability layer provides NO confidentiality guarantees. Any CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB/2 cells are sufficient to reconstruct the entire blob.

reachability.notes: This is a design property, not a vulnerability. Blob submitters should not expect confidentiality from the data availability layer.

properties.severity_justification: Design property. Blob data is publicly available by design once included in a block.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Not a vulnerability. Documented design property of PeerDAS.

properties.text: The computational cost of recover_polynomialcoeff (SG-023) is inherently O(n log n) for FFT operations and O(k^2) for vanishing polynomial construction (k = number of missing cells, bounded by CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2). An attacker who controls which columns to withhold can maximize k up to the 50% threshold.

reachability.notes: Computational cost is bounded and deterministic but could be significant for maximum k. This is an inherent property of the algorithm, not a bug.

properties.severity_justification: Computational DoS bounded by 50% threshold. Maximum cost is deterministic and implementation-dependent.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Conditional scope: inherent algorithmic complexity, not an implementation bug. High-effort DoS is out-of-scope per program rules.

properties.text: The Execution Layer data received via Engine API (engine_getBlobsV2) is authenticated via JWT. However, if the EL is compromised, corrupted blob data would propagate into the polynomial commitment pipeline. CL implementations SHOULD verify blob KZG commitments against blob data received from EL.

reachability.notes: EL is semi-trusted (JWT-authenticated). Compromised EL could inject corrupted blobs. CL should verify blob-to-commitment correspondence.

properties.severity_justification: Requires compromised co-located EL. Corrupted blobs would produce invalid cells and proofs, caught by receiving validators during verification.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires compromised EL which is not directly attacker-controlled from outside.

properties.text: compute_cells (SG-018) MUST produce exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells, where each cell represents polynomial evaluations over a distinct coset. The input blob MUST be exactly BYTES_PER_BLOB bytes.

reachability.notes: compute_cells is used in cells_and_kzg_proofs_construction (Validator SG-002). Incorrect cell count causes sidecar construction failures.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect cell count from compute_cells would be caught by downstream assertions in sidecar construction.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate incorrect cell count causing downstream failures.

properties.text: The kzg_commitments_inclusion_proof in DataColumnSidecar MUST be verified against the block's Merkle root by receiving validators. In get_data_column_sidecars_from_block (Validator SG-004), the proof is computed from the actual block; in get_data_column_sidecars_from_column_sidecar (Validator SG-005), the proof is reused from the input sidecar and MUST have been previously verified.

reachability.notes: Without Merkle proof verification, an attacker can link sidecars to arbitrary blocks, corrupting the data availability state.

properties.severity_justification: Missing Merkle proof verification allows sidecars to be attributed to wrong blocks, breaking data availability tracking.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that missing Merkle proof verification allows sidecar attribution to non-existent block.

properties.text: A delayed withholding attack where a block proposer publishes valid sidecars but delays publication to some subnets MUST be mitigated by attestation deadlines, fork choice rules, and the 50% Reed-Solomon redundancy. Validators MUST NOT finalize blocks where data availability cannot be confirmed within the attestation window.

reachability.notes: Strategic delay within the attestation window is hard to distinguish from network latency. The 50% redundancy ensures partial availability is sufficient for recovery.

properties.severity_justification: Delayed withholding can cause temporary finality delays but is bounded by attestation window and redundancy. Cannot cause permanent consensus failure.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate measurable finality delay from strategic delayed withholding.

properties.text: The divide_polynomialcoeff function MUST correctly implement polynomial long division: a = quotient * b + remainder. The remainder is discarded. The quotient degree MUST equal deg(a) - deg(b).

reachability.notes: Used in KZG proof computation (SG-014) to compute quotient polynomial. Incorrect division produces invalid proofs.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect polynomial division produces invalid KZG proofs for all computed cells.

properties.text: The multiply_polynomialcoeff function MUST produce a result of degree deg(a) + deg(b). The product polynomial MUST satisfy: for any z, evaluate(result, z) == evaluate(a, z) * evaluate(b, z).

reachability.notes: Used in vanishing polynomial construction and interpolation. Incorrect multiplication corrupts recovery and proof computation.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect polynomial multiplication corrupts vanishing polynomial and interpolation. Not directly attacker-triggered.

properties.text: The interpolation polynomial computed by interpolate_polynomialcoeff MUST satisfy: for all i, evaluate(result, xs[i]) == ys[i]. The result degree MUST be at most len(xs) - 1.

reachability.notes: Interpolation is used in batch verification (SG-015) to compute sum_interp. Incorrect interpolation corrupts the verification equation.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect interpolation in verification equation could cause false acceptance or rejection of proofs.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that interpolation error in batch verification causes incorrect verification result.

properties.text: P2P request rate limiting MUST be implemented for data column sidecar requests during the retention period. Validators SHOULD implement request throttling per peer to prevent resource exhaustion from excessive requests.

reachability.notes: Excessive requests flood storage I/O and network bandwidth. Bounded by retention period limiting historical range. Rate limiting is implementation-dependent.

properties.severity_justification: Storage I/O and bandwidth exhaustion from excessive requests. Bounded by retention period and mitigated by per-peer throttling.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Conditional scope: high-effort single-peer DoS attacks are out-of-scope per program rules.

properties.text: The get_data_column_sidecars function MUST assert that len(cells_and_kzg_proofs) == len(kzg_commitments) as a precondition. If this assertion fails, sidecar construction MUST be aborted.

reachability.notes: Mismatch between cells_and_kzg_proofs and kzg_commitments could cause out-of-bounds access during sidecar construction.

properties.severity_justification: Mismatched lengths cause out-of-bounds during sidecar construction, crashing the proposer node.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate mismatch causing proposer crash during sidecar construction.

properties.text: The E(x) * Z(x) recovery in recover_polynomialcoeff MUST correctly handle the extended_evaluation_rbo construction: missing cells MUST be filled with zeros, and the bit-reversal permutation MUST be applied to produce the canonical evaluation ordering.

reachability.notes: Incorrect zero-filling for missing cells or wrong permutation corrupts the extended evaluation, producing an incorrect polynomial.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect extended evaluation construction produces wrong polynomial from recovery, corrupting all reconstructed cells and proofs.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that incorrect zero-filling pattern produces wrong recovery result.

properties.text: The signed_block in get_data_column_sidecars_from_block (Validator SG-004) MUST be a valid SignedBeaconBlock. The signed_block_header and kzg_commitments_inclusion_proof MUST be derived from the actual block, not constructed independently.

reachability.notes: Block header and Merkle proof must be derived from the actual block to ensure sidecars are correctly linked. This is an internal construction step.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrectly derived header or Merkle proof causes sidecars to fail verification at receiving nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Internal construction, not directly attacker-triggered.

properties.text: All cell_indices in recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs MUST be in the range [0, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB). Cell indices >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB MUST be rejected before processing.

reachability.notes: Out-of-bounds cell_indices cause incorrect coset computation and potential array out-of-bounds during recovery.

properties.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds cell_indices cause node crash via array out-of-bounds in coset computation during recovery.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate node crash from out-of-bounds cell_index in recovery input.

properties.text: Each cell provided to recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs MUST be exactly BYTES_PER_CELL bytes in length. Cells with incorrect lengths MUST be rejected before coset evaluation conversion.

reachability.notes: Incorrectly sized cells cause incorrect field element parsing in cell_to_coset_evals, corrupting recovery.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect cell size causes deserialization errors that should be caught by the assertion. If not caught, corrupts recovery.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that incorrectly sized cell bypasses validation and corrupts recovery.
